## Summary

closes #875 (labeled `bug`)

## Details

- When we use `gh issue create` with issue templates, the `labels` in a frontmatter will apply as well as the `name`.

### Example

With this issue template, do `gh issue create`

```yaml
---
name: Bug report
about: Create a report to help us improve
title: Bug report
labels: bug, help wanted

---
```

then

issue_context.title: Creating an issue from a template doesn't apply template labels to newly created issue
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

When creating an issue using `gh issue create` and selecting a template, the labels associated with that template are not assigned to the issue upon creation.

```
$ gh version
gh version 0.7.0 (2020-04-22)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v0.7.0
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. `gh issue create` (against a repo that has issue templates with labels associated with each)
2. Fill in info
3. Create issue without previewing in browser
4. Observe that issue was not assigned labels associated with template that was chosen

### Expected vs actual behavior

If a template was chosen that has labels, those labels should be assigned to the issue when created via `gh issue create`

### Logs

```console
$ gh issue create

Creating issue in intel/dffml

? Choose a template Missing Documentation
? Title docs: cli: edit command
? Body <Received>
? What's next? Submit
https://github.com/intel/dffml/issues/616
```
comments:
Thank you for reporting!

To my team: I think this would be solved by passing the `issueTemplate` parameter (a new API under the `gh_cli` flag) to the `createIssue` GraphQL mutation.

review_comments:
Hi, thank you for attempting to solve this, but this solution is not going to work for anyone who fills in a template but does not have write or triage access to a repository. Most folks who open issues in open source repositories will  usually _not_ have privileges to assign arbitrary labels.

However, while filling out issues via web UI, some labels might be inherited from the template that was used. We definitely want this functionality in CLI as well, but for that we would need to pass the template name to the issue create GraphQL mutation. Currently, the API for that is _private_ to us, so we can not ask you to try to use that in this PR. For now I will close this and someone from our team is going to pick up the original issue soon and work on making this happen.

Thanks again!
